text:
li: quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA kernel selection RFC — found a few runtime safety invariants we should gate before we enable grouped-query on quantized paths. want to sync on tradeoffs and a rollout plan.

maya: +1. can you list the invariants? short bullets pls.

li: sure — top-level: 1) correctness under partial-KV-prefetch (no token corruption), 2) bounded latency variance for mixed-length groups, 3) deterministic fallback path when a kernel fails / OOM. also need to check that the grouped kernels respect per-request tracing/span boundaries.

jonah: on (1) — i hit a case where prefetch interleaving caused stale KV lookups for seq-len 1 in a 4-item group. reproducible in the perf lab.

li: interesting, can you paste the minimal repro?

jonah: repro snippet: ```python
# group of queries: [1, 32, 128, 16]
# prefetched KV offset used incorrectly for idx=0
for q in grouped: run_step(q)
```
behavior: first item sometimes reads previous group's cache if group boundary not flushed.

sam: that sounds like a collector-invariant: "flush KV on group boundary unless affinity==true". But flushing every boundary kills perf. we need a heuristic.

maya: what about tagging requests with `group_affinity_id` so runtime can keep small ephemeral caches per-affinity and only flush on affinity change?

li: i like that. provides safety and keeps perf for sticky groups. downside: needs API surface or implicit runtime-generated affinity tokens which complicates telemetry.

jonah: another risk — quantized kernels sometimes do internal reorder for vector widths. grouping exposes misaligned memory accesses under F32->INT8 shim. we need an assertion in the kernel adapter: if quantized && grouping_enabled then require aligned_batch_size mod 8 == 0 or fallback.

sam: fallback policy idea: runtime policy enum `GroupFallback = {DEGROUP, SPLIT_BY_LEN, FALLBACK_KERNEL}`. default = SPLIT_BY_LEN (max per-subgroup 32 tokens).

li: agreed. prefer conservative default. implement simple cost model: if grouping causes any kernel to violate alignment/assertion -> choose fallback according to policy.

infra-bot: perf-lab: build/2079 completed. grouped-query unit tests: 452 passed, 3 flaky. see CI run: https://ci.redwood/2079

eval-bot: eval suite: grouped vs single for RP-3 prompt set: latency p95 +22% when naive flush on every boundary, -12% when affinity-preserved. quality delta negligible.

maya: we should codify interface: 1) runtime-only flag `groupable: boolean` on Request metadata, 2) `group_affinity_id: string?` optional, 3) `grouping_hints: {max_subgroup_len:int, prefer_alignment:bool}` optional. Keep SDK change minimal: default omission = runtime decides.

li: to minimize SDK churn, let's make `group_affinity_id` optional and generated by runtime if absent and if request comes from same session token within 250ms. that gives sticky groups for chat flows.

jonah: sounds fine. need tests: microbenchmark for mixed-length distribution, and fuzz to catch KV prefetch race. i'll own that.

sam: i'll implement the fallback enum + alignment asserts in the kernel adapter. will add metrics: `group_fallback.reason` tag.

li: action items: @jonah microbench + fuzz (ETA Tue), @sam kernel-adapter fallback + metrics (ETA Wed), @maya draft SDK/telemetry note (ETA Thu). i'll update the RFC with the invariants and new rollout plan.

maya: thanks — can we add a small Canary plan? e.g., 1) enable grouping for internal-prod traffic only, 2) monitor `group_fallback.rate` and `latency.p95` for 24h, 3) expand to 10% external, then 100%.

li: yes — will add that. final Q: do we need an explicit opt-out in console per-model for grouped kernels?

sam: recommend default ON for models with verified grouping compatibility; console toggle per-model makes sense for enterprise.

li: sweet. i'll push a short RFC update this afternoon and ping for reviews. thanks all. :party-parrot:
